correctness.rationale: A generic diagonal one-parameter subgroup separates ambient coordinate monomials. The tangential variety is contained in the second secant variety, so every multigraded catalecticant has rank at most two. For a monomial, local catalecticant ranks are coefficients of the divisor generating polynomial; support at least three forces first-catalecticant rank at least three, while two support variables with both exponents at least two force second-catalecticant rank at least three. Hence the only non-pure local possibilities are x_a x_b in degree two and x_a^(d-1)x_b in degree at least three. Tensor-product flattening ranks multiply, excluding non-pure behavior in two factors simultaneously. The surviving monomials are explicitly tangent directions, so the fixed-locus classification is exact. Euler localization then gives the count. The packaged checker independently reconstructs all these ranks on mixed finite grids.

value.rationale: Tangential Segre--Veronese varieties are basic partially symmetric tensor varieties, and the archival literature studies their rank and decomposition geometry. The formula supplies a canonical global topological invariant uniformly for any number of factors and exposes a sharp and simple degree-threshold law: each factor contributes differently only at degrees one and two, then stabilizes from degree three onward. The mixed formula simultaneously explains and extends the pure Segre and Veronese boundary cases, while the quadratic correction is structurally forced by symmetry rather than by an arbitrary parameter slice.
